text:
Troy Terry made his season debut on Nov. 11, after missing Anaheim's first month, and joined a Ducks team that TSN was already calling red-hot. Five games in, he has 2 assists and no goals on six shots, playing about 14 minutes a night, roughly four and a half fewer than his usual role.

It's way too early to judge. The Ducks have been out-chanced at five on five with him on the ice in those games, and they've also scored about three fewer goals than expected while he's out there, so the small sample has been unkind both ways. Our talent range still puts his true scoring rate between about 2.3 and 3.3 points per 60 minutes, close to the 57 points he scored last season.

Evolving-Hockey had him at the 94th percentile among forwards for driving play last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries and setting up shots at the 85th percentile. That's a first-line playmaker. What we'd watch is how fast his minutes climb back toward the top six.
headline: Troy Terry is back, and the Ducks didn't wait for him
